explanation: The Sun's gravity adds to the effect. When Sun and Moon line up, at new and full moon, their pulls combine into extra-high spring tides, named for springing up, not for the season.

claims.text: The ocean tides are caused mainly by the Moon's gravity.
Earth's rotation on its own, the wind and the Sun's heat do not cause the tides.
The Sun's gravity also contributes to the tides.
Spring tides, with the largest tidal range, occur around new and full moon, when the Sun and Moon line up.
The name spring tide comes from the idea of the water springing up, not from the season.
